newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland likely to meet EMU criteria in 2006 - c.bank.
newsitem.headline: Poland likely to meet EMU criteria in 2006 - c.bank.

text.p: Poland is likely to meet the criteria of entry into the Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) in 2006 after it brings inflation down to the required level, the central bank president said on Tuesday.

Hanna Gronkiewicz-Waltz also said next year's budget gap was likely to shrink to 1.7 percent of gross domestic product from the current 2.8 percent, while the year-on-year inflation rate was expected to fall to 9.5 percent in 1998.
Polish inflation stood at 15.3 percent in April and was expected to fall to around 13 percent by the end of 1997.
Gronkiewicz-Waltz told a seminar on EMU that in order to achieve the EMU entry goal Poland needed not only to conduct tight monetary policy but also a rigid fiscal policy.
"It is quite realistic that we will have a smaller budget gap and single digit inflation next year," she said.
She said Poland may expect a balanced budget in 1999 or the year 2000 even though the introduction of pension reform would make spending cuts difficult.
Gronkiewicz-Waltz stressed the need to speed up structural reforms of the economy, mainly privatisation, and the need to control wage growth to keep inflation in check.

She said the NBP may be forced to intervene on the market more often from the year 2002 -- the expected date of Poland's accession to the European Union (EU) -- to keep the zloty rate within the agreed EMU band of plus/minus 15 percent from the parity rate.

Gronkiewicz-Waltz said the fall in inflation this year was mainly a result of changes in the structure of financing the budget deficit, as the central bank was no longer obliged to lend money to the treasury.

She said the main sources of inflation in Poland were wage indexation, pensions and of budget spending, market protection, in terms of duties on grains and other products, state monopolies in many areas of industry and price inertia.
